claim:
Let \(X=\mathrm{ces}_3^{(2)}\) be \(\mathbb R^2\) with
\[
\|(x,y)\|_X=
\left(
|x|^3+\left(\frac{|x|+|y|}{2}\right)^3
\right)^{1/3}.
\]
Let \(\tau>0\) be the unique solution of
\[
3^{4/3}(1+\tau)^2
=
\tau\bigl((1+\tau)^2+8\bigr).
\]
Then the classical von Neumann--Jordan constant is
\[
C_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X)
=
\frac{\bigl(8+(1+\tau)^3\bigr)^{2/3}}
{3^{4/3}+\tau^2}
=
1.29958204360103898476109693949\ldots .
\]
An extremizing pair is
\[
x=(1,0),\qquad y=(0,\tau).
\]
integrity: The proof independently derives a sharp global Hilbert comparison from an exhaustive one-variable optimization and then gives an exact extremizing pair for the classical von Neumann--Jordan ratio. Numerical values are consistency checks only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to the real two-dimensional Cesàro space at exponent 3. It does not give a formula for all p>2 or for higher-dimensional Cesàro spaces. An equivalent later computation under different notation remains a residual bibliographic risk.
title: Exact von Neumann--Jordan constant of the cubic two-dimensional Cesàro space
